blocks: Integrity Checklist for National Delegations to COP

The UNFCCC Conference of the Parties (COP) is the world’s foremost decision-making arena for addressing the climate crisis. To maintain trust in multilateral climate action, it is vital that national delegations demonstrate transparency, accountability, and integrity in their composition and conduct. This checklist helps governments strengthen the credibility of their COP delegations, preventing undue influence, and enhancing the legitimacy and effectiveness of global climate negotiations. The checklist applies to all participants in national delegations and under party overflow.
1. Representatives from High-Polluting Industries
CHECKBOX ☐ Avoid appointing delegates who are affiliated with fossil fuel companies and other

• high polluting industries whose core business is incompatible with the goals of the Paris Agreement. Their presence delegitimises National Delegations and raises concerns on the undue influence of high polluters contrary to the goals of the Paris Agreement and the purpose of COPs.
CHECKBOX ☐ Establish a process with clear criteria for selecting participation in Delegations and
• Party Overflow, including emphasis on civil society representation, gender and social inclusion, and sectors and industries demonstrating track record and commitment to Paris Agreement goals.
CHECKBOX ☐ Establish clear conflict of interest rules to prevent individuals with ties to major
• polluting industries from influencing negotiations in ways that undermine climate ambition.
2. Transparency of Delegates and their Affiliations
• CHECKBOX ☐ Well ahead of COP, publish a full, up-to-date list of all delegates in national delegation, and participants holding “party overflow badges.”
CHECKBOX ☐ Ahead of COP publish all affiliations of all participants to fossil fuel and other high

• polluting industries, be it private other state-owned entities, including (but not limited to) shareholders/owners, members of board of other supervisory/governance/ body; leadership positions; consultancy contracts and unpaid adviserships.
CHECKBOX ☐ Ensure that the above information is made available both domestically and
• through the UNFCCC Secretariat’s official channels.
3. Code of Conduct
CHECKBOX ☐ Require all delegation and party overflow members to sign a code of conduct that

• emphasizes transparency, integrity, respect for the principles of the UNFCCC process. Include explicit commitments to: Act in all engagements with the overriding interest of meeting Paris Agreement goals; Avoid conflicts of interest especially with fossil fuel industries; Declaring all relevant current and former affiliations with fossil fuel and other high polluting industries.
CHECKBOX ☐ Internal procedures and processes are established for addressing breaches of
• the code of conduct, including removal from delegations if necessary.
By implementing this checklist, national delegations reduce risks of undue influence and ensure effective COPs, reflecting the interests of people and the planet for meeting Paris Agreement Goals.
